featured_reviews.name: Diago Fernandes
featured_reviews.review_text:
Extremely Disappointing Experience.

My experience at Ramakrishna Mission Hospital was deeply unsatisfactory and alarming. For an institution associated with such a respected name, the overall standards of care, hygiene, and management are far below acceptable levels.

The trainee doctors displayed an arrogant, careless, and dismissive attitude, lacking basic empathy and professionalism. Patient concerns were often brushed aside, creating unnecessary stress and frustration.

Cleanliness is a major issue throughout the hospital. Washrooms and patient areas were unhygienic, poorly maintained, and visibly dirty, raising serious concerns about infection control and patient safety.

Despite booking and paying for a “First Class” room, the condition was horrible and unacceptable—dirty floors, stained and broken tiles, poorly maintained toilets, foul smell, and an overall neglected environment. This was misleading and completely unworthy of a first-class facility.

Time management is extremely poor. Long waiting hours, lack of communication, and no respect for patients’ time indicate weak administration and poor coordination.

The only positive aspect of this hospital experience was the professionalism and dedication of Dr. Ulhas Nadkarni and Dr. Amarish Warty. Both doctors were knowledgeable, patient, and compassionate, and they treated us with respect and genuine care. Their conduct reflects what medical professionalism should look like.

Unfortunately, apart from these two doctors, the hospital suffers from poor hygiene, unprofessional trainee behavior, misleading facilities, and inefficient management. Immediate corrective action is required.

I would not recommend this hospital unless serious improvements are made.

I also brought the bottle of a prescription medication I’ve been taking for years, clearly labeled with my name, simply asking for a refill while traveling. Despite knowing me for less than five minutes, the doctor confidently informed me that I “shouldn’t take it” and refused to prescribe it.

Women's Hospital "Room Harmony" has been etched in my memory as it  was my home for two and a half months.

Healthcare should be fair and reasonable, especially when patients rely on insurance. In this case, the lack of transparency and the inflated billing makes it feel intentional rather than incidental.

Patients should be very cautious, insist on clarity upfront, and review every detail carefully before proceeding. It is always better to go for proper cashless processing wherever possible, consider alternative hospitals if things are unclear, and inform your insurance company in advance to avoid unnecessary financial burden later.

featured_reviews.name: jhalak gala
featured_reviews.review_text:
To,
The Management,
Sanjeevni Hospital, Andheri East

Subject: Serious Concerns Regarding Hospital Facilities, Staff Management & Patient Care

I am writing this feedback with deep disappointment regarding the overall experience and facilities provided during our patient’s admission for knee replacement surgery at your hospital.

There appears to be only 1 sister/nurse and 1 housekeeping staff managing 3 floors. In case of emergencies, even after ringing the bell repeatedly, the staff arrives extremely late — sometimes after nearly an hour. In a medical emergency, such delays can become life-threatening. The management seriously needs to address this issue immediately and appoint more staff for proper patient care and safety.

The cleanliness and maintenance standards of the hospital are also extremely poor. Rooms and patient areas were not cleaned properly, and hygiene was highly disappointing.

Food service was another major concern:
- Morning breakfast was either delayed or sometimes not provided at all.
- The quality of food served was extremely poor and difficult even for patients to consume.

The discharge process was unnecessarily lengthy and unorganized:
- Even after the doctor approved discharge, it took around 1.5 to 2 hours just to send the file to the billing counter.
- Thereafter, another 2 to 3 hours were wasted in completing billing and discharge formalities.
- Overall, discharge took almost 4 to 5 hours, causing unnecessary inconvenience to patients and their families.

The hospital also urgently requires:
- Better management systems
- More nursing and housekeeping staff
- Proper stretcher lifts
- Better food and qualified cooks
- Improved hygiene and room maintenance

Another highly disappointing aspect was that the doctor who performed the knee replacement surgery did not visit the patient even once during the entire 4-day admission period after surgery.

Additionally, hospital clothes provided to patients were not changed regularly. When requested for fresh clothes, the staff kept giving excuses such as “it is in laundry.” This is unacceptable for admitted patients who require proper hygiene and care.

Overall, the experience was extremely disappointing and far below expected healthcare standards. The hospital management seriously needs to improve patient care, staffing, cleanliness, food quality, emergency response time, and administrative efficiency.

We hope this feedback is taken seriously and immediate corrective measures are implemented so that future patients and their families do not face similar difficulties.

Regards,
Damyanti Gala
